Keep the rest of mod.rs as it is (line timing, affine reference points, accessors, render_line's layer collection). Other workers own obj.rs, bg_affine.rs and bitmap.rs.

Contract (on main, commit "refactor(ppu): layer line contract"):
- `compose_line(&mut self, line, layers: &LineLayers)`. `LineLayers` holds `backgrounds[4]` and `background_enabled[4]`, `sprites` (front-most sprite pixel per x, with OBJ `priority` and `is_semi_transparent_sprite`), `sprites_enabled` (DISPCNT OBJ on) and `obj_window[240]` (pixels inside the OBJ window).
- Each layer's `color` is BGR555 and `priority` 0-3; transparent pixels have `is_transparent`.
- Helpers: `ppu.register(offset)` gives raw WIN0H/WIN1H/WIN0V/WIN1V/WININ/WINOUT/MOSAIC/BLDCNT/BLDALPHA/BLDY; `dispcnt()`; `palette_color(0)` is the backdrop.

Scope:
- Windows 0/1, the OBJ window and the outside area. Each controls layer enables and the colour special effect enable. Handle window coordinate edge cases: x2 > 240 or x1 > x2, the same for y (gbatek: LCD I/O Window Feature).
- Colour special effects: alpha blending with EVA/EVB, brightness increase and decrease with EVY. First and second targets include the backdrop. A semi-transparent sprite always alpha-blends when the pixel below it is a second target, regardless of BLDCNT mode (gbatek: LCD I/O Color Special Effects).
- BG mosaic (gbatek: LCD I/O Mosaic Function). Implement it as a post-pass on each BG's `[LayerPixel; 240]` inside compose or a helper, horizontal and vertical, using BGxCNT bit 6. If vertical mosaic needs the renderers to sample a different line, describe that as a contract change for the integrator instead of editing mod.rs's render_line. OBJ mosaic belongs to the sprites worker.
- Priority: lower value wins; a sprite beats a BG of the same priority; BG0 beats BG3 on ties.
Keep it fast: no per-line allocation, per pixel only simple integer math.

- Unit tests.
- Dev ROMs via run_rom: $GBA_EVAL/corpus/roms/test/tonc/win-demo.gba, tonc/bld-demo.gba, tonc/mos-demo.gba, tonc/prio-demo.gba, destoer/window-midframe.gba ($GBA_EVAL=/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-eval). Sprites are a stub on your branch, so judge BG-only parts.

<result>I built the line compositor, but grading is unfinished: both grading runs (main 4e3eddf and my branch) were stopped by the system for low memory while the session sat idle. I was told not to restart them, so I have no summary.json. The scores below are the per-frame match values (`replay_score_deduped`) from the per-test JSON files the runs wrote before they died. `cargo test` passes (102 tests, 4 of them new) and the wasm release build succeeds.

## 1. What I built and the commits
Branch `phase3/ppu-effects`, from 4e3eddf:
- `12147f0` feat(ppu): windows, colour effects, BG mosaic in line compositor
- `1a484a6` fix(ppu): OBJ window needs DISPCNT OBJ enable too

The compositor now lives in `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/.claude/worktrees/agent-a74f182e8b7063d5e/src/ppu/effects.rs` as `impl Ppu { pub(super) fn compose_line }`. There are no per-line allocations, and each pixel only does integer compares and shifts.
- **Windows:** window 0, then window 1, then the OBJ window, then the outside area. A garbage end value (X2>240 or X1>X2, the same for Y with 160) is read as the screen edge. Each region's bits gate the BG and OBJ layers and the effects bit. When no window is on, everything is enabled.
- **Priority:** the compositor keeps the front two pixels, sorting on `priority*8 + order`, where OBJ is 0 and BG0-BG3 are 1-4. So lower priority wins, a sprite beats a BG of the same priority, and BG0 beats BG3 on ties. The backdrop is a target in both slots.
- **Effects:** alpha blending with EVA/EVB and brightness increase/decrease with EVY. Coefficients 17-31 count as 16. A semi-transparent sprite blends whenever the pixel under it is a second target, whatever the BLDCNT mode. If it doesn't blend, normal BLDCNT handling applies (for example brightness, if OBJ is a first target).
- **BG mosaic:** horizontal mosaic reads the pixel at `x - x % width`. For vertical mosaic, the first line of each block is copied into a new `Ppu` field, `mosaic_source_lines: [[LayerPixel; 240]; 4]` (about 6 KB), and reused for the rest of the block.

The only changes to `mod.rs` are: the old `compose_line` is removed, that field and its initial value are added, and the now-unneeded `#[allow(dead_code)]` on `register()` is dropped.

Dev ROMs, driven with key input through a throwaway runner in the scratchpad:
- **bld-demo:** alpha blending (EVA 8 / EVB 7), brightness increase and brightness decrease all look right on the BG.
- **mos-demo:** BG mosaic looks right for vertical-only and for horizontal plus vertical.
- **win-demo:** the window rectangle shows correctly.
- **prio-demo:** looks plausible; sprites are a stub on this branch.
- **window-midframe:** draws, but there is no reference image to check it against.

## 2. Scores, before (main 4e3eddf) and after (this branch)
| Test | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| piugba-gameplay | 0.3233 | **0.9390** (diverging frames 1918 to 1635) |
| tonc-snd1 | 0.9167 | 0.9167 |
| aw-arm-alu | 0.8311 | 0.8311 |
| aw-thumb-alu | 0.8328 | 0.8328 |
| memory | 1.0 | 1.0 |
| timer-reload | 0.5396 | 0.5396 |
| dma-priority | 0.9784 | 0.9784 |
| bulletgba-gameplay | 0.6684 | not reached |
| spout-gameplay, celeste-gameplay, goodboy-gameplay | not reached | not reached |

No smoke-set test changed. The remaining four games still need grading once memory allows: `scripts/grade-subset.sh target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/gba_emu.wasm p3-effects spout-gameplay bulletgba-gameplay celeste-gameplay goodboy-gameplay`. Eight grader containers from other workers were running at the same time, which is the likely cause.

## 3. Unfinished work, guesses and contract changes
- **Mid-frame vertical windows:** gbatek doesn't say what happens when WIN0V/WIN1V change during a frame, so each line is checked on its own against Y1..Y2. window-midframe may want latched behaviour instead.
- **Vertical mosaic shortcut:** the first line of a block is reused exactly as it was drawn, so scroll or affine changes partway through a block are ignored. Doing it exactly would be a contract change: render_line would pass the renderers the block's first line (`line - line % height`) for BGs with mosaic on, and the compositor would only apply horizontal mosaic.
- **OBJ window enable:** I followed gbatek's "Both DISPCNT Bits 12 and 15 must be set", so the OBJ window only counts when OBJ display is on. The comment in render_line says the opposite. If the reference disagrees, it's a one-line change (`obj_window_on`).
- **Effects-disabled windows:** I guessed that turning effects off in a window region also stops semi-transparent sprites from blending there.
- **Contract changes needed:** none that are required. The vertical-mosaic one above is optional.

## 4. Decisions for NOTES.md (2026-11-05)
- The compositor moved into effects.rs as an `impl Ppu` method, to keep the Phase 3 code in one owned file.
- Vertical BG mosaic reuses a stored copy of each block's first line, which avoids changing the renderer contract. Its limit is described in section 3.
- The OBJ window requires both DISPCNT bits 12 and 15, following gbatek.
- Windows are decided per line with no state carried between lines, since gbatek describes no latching.
- A semi-transparent sprite that has no second target below it falls through to normal BLDCNT handling.</result>

## 1. What I built and the commits

- `c04db04 fix(apu): halve DAC to i16 scale to match reference level and avoid clipping`
- `9070d5f feat(apu): direct sound FIFOs, mixer and SOUNDBIAS DAC output`

**`/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/.claude/worktrees/agent-a4ec101f887cf580c/src/apu/fifo.rs`**
- Each FIFO holds 32 bytes. Writes to FIFO_A/FIFO_B (0x0A0-0x0A7) push the bytes the write mask selects, low byte first, so 8-, 16- and 32-bit writes all work.
- Each timer overflow moves one byte to the output, and that sample is held until the next overflow. If the FIFO is empty, the last sample keeps playing.
- After each pop it reports a refill when 16 bytes or fewer remain. The reset bit empties the FIFO and sets its output to 0.

**`/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/.claude/worktrees/agent-a4ec101f887cf580c/src/apu/mod.rs`**
- **Timer overflows:** `on_timer_overflow` pops from each FIFO whose SOUNDCNT_H timer select matches, but only while the master enable is on. It returns the refill mask.
- **PSG mixing:** each channel level (-15..15) is multiplied by the SOUNDCNT_L master volume + 1. It is then reduced for the SOUNDCNT_H ratio (25/50/100%) and added left and right according to the enable bits.
- **FIFO mixing:** each FIFO sample is multiplied by 4 at 100% volume or by 2 at 50%, giving the +/-0x200 range gbatek describes.
- **DAC output:** the sum plus the bias is clipped to 0..0x3FF. The low bits the selected resolution cannot output are dropped. The bias is then subtracted and the result shifted left 5 to give the i16 sample. If the master enable is off, the output is silence.
- **SOUNDCNT_H:** the FIFO reset bits (11 and 15) act on write and are not stored.
- **SOUNDCNT_X:** reads return the stored bit 7 plus `psg.active_channels()`. When bit 7 goes from 1 to 0, it calls `psg.power_off()` and clears SOUNDCNT_L.
- **Sample rate:** `sample_rate()` and the sample count per frame follow 32768 << SOUNDBIAS bits 14-15. Each sample takes exactly 16777216 / rate cycles (512, 256, 128 or 64), so the count never drifts. On the dev ROMs, 300 frames gave exactly 164587 samples at 32768 Hz.
- **Unit tests:** FIFO byte order, byte writes, refill threshold and reset; FIFO-to-mixer output; the sample count at 262 kHz; DAC clipping.

## 2. Scores

| Test | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| celeste-gameplay audio | 0.0 | 0.8857 (0.8858 at shift 6) |
| piugba-gameplay audio | 0.0 | 0.6840 (0.6799 at shift 6) |
| aw-arm-alu, aw-thumb-alu, memory, timer-reload, dma-priority | video 1.0 | 1.0 |
| tonc-snd1 | video 0.9917, audio 0.0 | 0.9917, 0.0 |

- tonc-snd1 audio stays at 0 because the PSG is still a stub; that is the PSG worker's file.
- I ran the full smoke set at shift 6 and only the two graded games after the shift-5 commit. The shift only changes audio level, so it cannot affect the video-only smoke tests.
- Both dev ROMs produce non-silent audio.

## 3. Unfinished work, guesses and contract changes

- **Output level:** the shift of 5 came from comparing against the reference WAVs, which were about 2x quieter than ours. Celeste and piugba both showed the same ratio, so it is not tuned to one game.
- **piugba length:** our output is 957 samples (about 1.7 frames) longer than the reference. The loudness over time otherwise tracks the reference closely, so the offset probably comes from frame or boot alignment outside my files.
- **Where gbatek is unclear, I guessed:**
  - Bytes written to a full FIFO are dropped.
  - An empty FIFO keeps playing its last sample.
  - FIFOs only pop while the master enable is on.
  - Refill requests go out whatever the left/right enable bits are, so an empty FIFO B on the same timer also gets one. The DMA ignores it unless a channel targets FIFO B.
  - SOUNDCNT_H ratio value 3 ("prohibited") is treated as 100%.
  - PSG register writes are not blocked while the master enable is off; gbatek doesn't say they should be.
- **Contract changes:** none needed.

## 4. Decisions for NOTES.md

- 2026-11-05: mixer works in gbatek's DAC units (each FIFO +/-0x200, each PSG channel about +/-0x80, plus bias, clipped to 10 bits, low bits dropped per resolution). Why: it follows the "Max Output Levels" section directly.
- 2026-11-05: i16 sample = (DAC value - bias) << 5. Subtracting the bias makes silence 0 even when a game sets bias 0. Shift 5 matches the reference WAV level, which was about 2x below shift 6, and avoids clipping.
- 2026-11-05: refill request is raised when a FIFO holds 16 bytes or fewer after a pop, for every FIFO on the overflowing timer. Why: gbatek says "only 4 x 32bits"; the DMA filters by destination address.</result>

<result>I reviewed `phase4/apu-fifo-mixer` (commits `9070d5f`, `c04db04`) against `main`. The branch changes only `src/apu/fifo.rs` and `src/apu/mod.rs`, which PLAN.md gives to the "FIFO + mixer" agent. Nothing in it branches on a particular ROM.

I checked the register handling against gbatek:
- **SOUNDCNT_L:** the volume bits (0-2 and 4-6) and the per-channel left/right enables (bits 8-11 and 12-15) are read correctly.
- **SOUNDCNT_H:** the PSG ratio (bits 0-1), the A/B volume (bits 2-3), and the A/B left/right enable, timer select and reset bits (bits 8-15) are correct.
- **SOUNDBIAS:** the bias mask covers bits 1-9, and the resolution bits 14-15 drop 1 to 4 low bits (9-bit down to 6-bit output).
- **Levels and clipping:** each FIFO spans ±0x200 and each PSG channel about ±0x80 (15 × 8 = 120), matching "Max Output Levels". The sum plus bias is clipped to 0..0x3FF.
- **FIFO refill and timers:** a DMA refill is requested when 16 bytes or fewer remain. Only timers 0 and 1 drive the FIFOs.
- **Master disable:** clearing SOUNDCNT_X bit 7 resets the PSG registers, and channel status bits 0-3 read back from the PSG.

`cargo test` passed (116 tests) and the wasm release build succeeded. As instructed, I did not run the grader. I ran `run_rom` for 300 frames on `gba-sound-demo-rates.gba` and `gba-sound-demo-song.gba`. Both produced non-silent audio at 32768 Hz with no clipping (peaks were -16384 to 16256).

Findings:

- `src/apu/mod.rs:160`: [minor] PSG and SOUNDCNT_L writes still go through while the master enable is off. gbatek (SOUNDCNT_X) says registers 0x060-0x081 are reset and "must not be written", and only 0x082 and 0x088 stay writable. Suggested fix: in `io_write16`, ignore writes to 0x060-0x081 (but not wave RAM) while `master_enabled()` is false.
- `src/apu/mod.rs:165`: [minor] The magic offsets `0x0A2` and `0x0A6` are used for the upper halves of FIFO_A and FIFO_B. Suggested fix: add `FIFO_A_HIGH` and `FIFO_B_HIGH` constants with comments, or match on `offset & !2`.
- `src/apu/mod.rs:110`, `:119`, `:141`: [minor] Raw bit positions in SOUNDCNT_L and SOUNDCNT_H have no names: `0x0100 << channel`, `0x1000 << channel`, `>> (8 + 4 * fifo_index)`, `& 1` and `& 2` as right/left, `4 << fifo_index`, and `>> (10 + 4 * fifo_index)`. Suggested fix: small named helpers or constants such as `fifo_enabled_right(index)` and `fifo_timer_select(index)`, or at least one comment per bit field.
- `src/apu/mod.rs:182`: [minor] Unused bits 4-7 of SOUNDCNT_H are stored and read back. Suggested fix: mask them out of `stored_mask`.
- `src/apu/mod.rs:82`: [minor] `master_enabled` has no doc comment. It is a trivial function, so this is optional.
- `src/apu/mod.rs:36` (`DAC_TO_I16_SHIFT = 5`): [minor] The scale to i16 was chosen to match the grader's reference level (commit `c04db04`). That is an allowed source and not a per-ROM hack, but the comment should say it is an output-level choice that gbatek does not define.
- Outside this branch, `src/gba.rs:79-85` (integrator's file): one `timers.step` call can report many overflows, and they are all popped before any DMA refill runs. At high timer rates or with large step sizes the FIFO could run dry within one step. Worth checking during integration if the celeste or piugba audio sounds choppy.

VERDICT: merge
ORIGINALITY: clean

The code reads as written from gbatek's register tables and Max Output Levels section. The names and structure match the rest of the codebase, and I saw no tables or comments pointing to another emulator.</result>

- **SOUNDCNT_L:** the volume bits (0-2 and 4-6) and the per-channel left/right enables (bits 8-11 and 12-15) are read correctly.

- **FIFO refill and timers:** a DMA refill is requested when 16 bytes or fewer remain. Only timers 0 and 1 drive the FIFOs.

All four PSG channels now work. `tonc-snd1` audio went from 0.0 to 0.98. `chip-advance-gameplay` stays at 0.842, but my channels don't affect it: that score comes entirely from the FIFO/mixer work. The final scores below come from the real mixer after merging `main` (b48003c), not from a throwaway merge.

### 1. What I built and the commits
Everything is in `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/.claude/worktrees/agent-ad48c768da4b9ac2b/src/apu/psg.rs`, on branch `phase4/apu-psg`. The contract signatures are unchanged.

- **Frame sequencer:** runs at 512 Hz (every 32768 cycles). It drives length at 256 Hz, sweep at 128 Hz and envelope at 64 Hz. `step()` cuts the elapsed cycles at sequencer ticks and moves each channel's frequency timer forward with div/mod, so there is no per-cycle loop. Only the noise LFSR loops, once per shift.
- **Channels 1 and 2:** four duty patterns, 64-step length, envelope, and the trigger bit (only when the mask says that byte was really written). Channel 1 also has sweep, including the overflow check when the sound restarts and after each sweep step; going past 2047 switches the channel off.
- **Channel 3:** two 16-byte wave RAM banks. The CPU reads and writes the bank that is not playing. It supports 32 or 64 digits (64 starts with the selected bank), volume 0/100/50/25%, the forced 75% bit, 256-step length, and the stop bit in `SOUND3CNT_L`.
- **Channel 4:** noise LFSR in 7-bit (start 0x40, XOR 0x60) or 15-bit (start 0x4000, XOR 0x6000) mode, using the divider and shift period from gbatek (r=0 treated as 0.5).
- **Outputs:** `channel_outputs()` gives +volume when the signal is high and -volume when low. Wave digits 0..15 are mapped to -15..15 before the volume is applied.
- **Status and power off:** `active_channels()` reports the four "playing" flags. `power_off()` resets everything except wave RAM.
- **Tests:** 5 unit tests covering duty and length stop, envelope, sweep overflow, the wave bank swap, and the 7-bit LFSR repeating after 127 steps.

Commits:
- `76f134e feat(apu): PSG channels 1-4 with frame sequencer`
- `e0f61d9 Merge branch 'main' into phase4/apu-psg` (your request)

`cargo test` passes (121 tests) and the wasm build is clean with no warnings.

### 2. Scores (audio, unless video is noted)
| test | before (silent mixer) | after |
|---|---|---|
| tonc-snd1 | 0.0 | **0.9815** |
| chip-advance-gameplay | 0.0 | 0.8423 |
| aw-arm-alu, aw-thumb-alu, memory, timer-reload, dma-priority | video 1.0 | video 1.0 (no regression) |

On why `chip-advance-gameplay` doesn't depend on the PSG:
- **Same score without my channels:** graded with the old stub `psg.rs` on top of `main`, it still scores 0.8423 (`tonc-snd1` drops to 0).
- **What the game writes:** I logged its sound register writes over the full replay. It writes only four PSG registers, and channel 3 is started at volume 0. Its music comes from the FIFOs, even though the testcase is labelled `psg`.

Any further gain on that test belongs to the mixer/FIFO side.

Two other things I checked:
- **Output level doesn't matter:** halving the PSG level in the mixer left both scores exactly the same.
- **What's left on tonc-snd1:** in the reference, notes start and change at slightly different times than in ours. The first note is about one frame later, and a later note change is about 170 samples later. The reference also looks high-pass filtered. That points to frame or CPU timing and output filtering, not to the channels.

### 3. Unfinished work, guesses and contract changes
- **Guess: silent envelope stops the channel.** If the envelope is volume 0 with direction "decrease", I switch the channel off (on trigger and when that register is written). gbatek only says "0=No Sound".
- **Guess: sweep time 0 waits 8 ticks.** gbatek only says time 0 disables sweep. I count it as 8 sequencer ticks before reloading.
- **Guess: length reload on restart.** When a sound restarts and its length counter has run out, the counter reloads to the full length (64, or 256 for channel 3).
- **Guess: sequencer runs while sound is off.** The frame sequencer starts at step 0 on reset and keeps running when the master enable is off.
- **Simplification: wave RAM.** gbatek describes wave RAM as a rotating shift register. I use a digit pointer instead, so a CPU read during playback returns the bytes in their unrotated positions.
- **Contract changes:** none needed.

### 4. Decisions worth logging in NOTES.md (2026-11-05)
- **PSG timing:** the frame sequencer is the 512 Hz clock, and frequency timers move forward with div/mod per call because HALT can pass thousands of cycles at once.
- **Output sign:** channel outputs are bipolar (±volume). The grader normalises level, so the mixer's PSG gain only matters relative to the FIFOs.
- **chip-advance is FIFO music:** its audio score depends on the FIFO/mixer, not the PSG (checked by grading with the stub and by logging register writes).
- **Remaining tonc-snd1 gap:** note timing and reference filtering, not the channels.</result>

| test | before review | after review |
|---|---|---|

| aw-arm-alu, aw-thumb-alu, memory, timer-reload, dma-priority | video 1.0 | video 1.0 |

- **Frame sequencer:** it now only divides 512 Hz down to the gbatek rates: length 256 Hz, sweep 128 Hz, envelope 64 Hz, each evenly spaced. The comment says the phase between them is arbitrary.
- **Sweep time 0:** no sweep at all, citing "Sweep is disabled by setting Sweep Time to zero". The reload-as-8 is gone.

- **2:** `Envelope::restart` now latches the step time and direction.
- **3:** resolved by removing both switch-off paths.
- **4:** comment added saying gbatek describes wave RAM as a 128-bit shift register and this code uses a position index.
- **5:** the stale `#[allow(dead_code)]` is gone.
- **6:** `///` comments naming the gbatek section are on all the helpers you listed, plus a new `sweep_time` helper. The noise output now lives in `NoiseChannel::output()`.

**7. Tests.** New tests cover:
- the length reload on restart after it ran out
- partial-byte NRx3/NRx4 writes (a low-byte write never restarts)
- the wave forced 75%, 50%, 25% and 0 volumes
- `power_off` keeping wave RAM

content.text:
Phase 4 is closed and tagged `phase-4`, with the replay-gate exception you approved. Nothing has been pushed.

**Score row** (commit `e551e06`):

| | Overall | Replay | Procedural | Audio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Phase 4 | **0.7976** | 0.7806 | 0.7611 | **0.8852** |
| Phase 3 | 0.6213 | 0.7818 | 0.7611 | 0.0000 |
| Baseline | 0.5345 | 0.596 | 0.486 | 0.399 |

- **Gate:**
  - Audio is 0.885, well above the 0.399 target.
  - Overall is 0.798, above Phase 3 and the baseline.
  - Replay is 0.0012 below Phase 3, all of it from spout's video (0.298 → 0.285). As you approved, this is accepted and logged in NOTES.md. The likely cause is that sound now uses DMA to refill its sample buffers, which takes CPU cycles and shifts spout's already-drifting timing.
- **Audio per replay:**
  - Strongest: collie-defense 0.996, bulletgba 0.974, varooom 0.964, goodboy 0.951, waimanu 0.912, celeste 0.886.
  - Middle: chip-advance 0.842, piugba 0.684.
  - Weakest: heartwrench 0.554, spout 0.199.
  - `tonc-snd1`: 0.981.
- **Sample rate:** `emu_audio_rate()` follows SOUNDBIAS (32768 << bits 14-15). At every rate the cycles per sample divide exactly, so the sample count doesn't drift.

**Agents** (all on claude-opus-5-5, each reviewed by a fresh reviewer):
- `apu-fifo-mixer` (1 review round): the two sample-buffer sound channels, the mixer, the SOUNDBIAS output stage and the sample rate.
- `apu-psg` (2 review rounds): the four tone, wave and noise channels. Round 1 flagged details that came from Game Boy documentation rather than gbatek. They were removed, and audio dropped by less than 0.0001.

**My own changes:**
- I fixed the interface between the two sound files on main before the workers started. The timer-to-sound-to-DMA events in `gba.rs` were already wired.
- The first full grade dropped `mgba-io-read` to 0.0025. The SOUNDCNT_X register reported channels with a permanently silent volume setting as playing, where the reference reports them off. I fixed that (reviewed twice; the first review caught a bug with 8-bit writes) and re-graded. The failed run was thrown away, not committed.
- Lesson logged: run the whole procedural set before a milestone, not only the phase's own tests.

**Still open:**
- Weakest replays for Phase 5: goodboy (video 0.08), spout (video 0.29, audio 0.20), heartwrench (video 0.58, audio 0.55), celeste (video 0.73). Phase 5 covers save hardware, timing and the cartridge prefetch buffer.
- piugba audio is 0.68. Our output runs about 957 samples longer than the reference, and the cause hasn't been found.
- Deferred minor review items are in NOTES.md, for example blocking writes to the sound registers while sound is switched off, and naming a few register bit constants.

Ready for Prompt 5.

Read CLAUDE.md, PLAN.md (Phase 5) and your agent definition; they are binding.

**Files you may edit (assigned by the integrator):** src/cpu/mod.rs, src/cpu/arm.rs, src/cpu/thumb.rs. This is the CPU instruction timing table. Two other workers own other files in parallel: one has ppu/bg_text.rs and ppu/effects.rs, the other has bus.rs (wait states, Game Pak prefetch) and cart.rs. Touch nothing else. If the cause is elsewhere, report it with evidence instead of editing.

**Integrator triage:** spout's intro screens match the reference. In gameplay it drifts out of sync. By frame 1500 the reference is still flying and ours shows "game over", and the luma error grows steadily from about frame 600. The input lands at fixed frames, so our game logic or physics runs at a different speed, or is seeded differently, than in Mesen2. The prime suspect is CPU cycle counts. Today decoders return internal cycles only, and `branch_to` charges no pipeline refill: gbatek "ARM CPU Instruction Cycle Times" says a branch costs 2S+1N, and IRQ entry, LDM/STM with PC, etc. also cost extra. A wrong cycle count makes the CPU do more work per frame than real hardware.
Implement the gbatek cycle times for your files: refill cycles on any PC write, exception entry costs, and the MUL/LDR/STR/LDM/STM internal cycles. The bus already charges S/N per access by address. The refill fetches should go through the bus so ROM wait states apply. Check that spout improves and nothing in the smoke set regresses. The timer-reload and timer-start-stop tests use delay constants tuned against current CPU timing, so if they drop, report it (don't edit timer.rs). Also check `memory`, `mgba-*` and `aw-*`.

<result>The bug is not in the PPU. It's in `src/dma.rs`, which is outside my files, so I made no code changes and there are no commits on `phase5/goodboy-gameplay`.

A one-line experiment in `src/dma.rs`, not committed, takes `goodboy-gameplay` video from **0.081 to 0.99999**. The worktree is back to clean `main` 9848efd.

## 1. Root cause
The game's level loader (Thumb code at ROM 0x08003A06–0x08003A24) starts a DMA3 copy and then cancels it in the very next instruction:
```
08003A20 LDR r1,=84000BC8      ; word size, immediate, enable, 0xBC8 words
08003A22 STR r1,[r2,#8]        ; DMA3CNT: start copying 0x08257404 -> 0x06008000
08003A24 STR r3,[r2,#8]        ; r3 = 0: DMA3CNT = 0
```
`Channel::latch` in `src/dma.rs` delays an immediate transfer by one whole CPU step (`start_delay_steps = 1`). So the `STR 0` at 3A24 runs before the transfer and cancels it. On hardware the DMA starts 2 cycles after enable (gbatek, DMA Transfers: "wait 2 clock cycles before accessing any DMA related registers"). The next instruction's code fetch from ROM takes longer than that, so the DMA has already taken the bus before the `STR 0` lands.

The evidence, from a throwaway probe that traced VRAM writes:
- On our side, 0x8000–0x94FF is the only part of BG1's tiles that ever gets written (168 tiles, from the earlier copy at 0x080039E2, which has an `LDR` between start and cancel).
- BG1's map at 0xB000 uses tile numbers up to 0x178, so tiles 0xA8–0x178 show whatever else is in VRAM there. That is the magenta and blue triangles.
- The VRAM at 0x8000 matches the ROM data byte for byte, BG1CNT stays 0x160B on every line, and `bg_text.rs` decodes correctly.

Yes. Phase 5 has raised the overall score from 0.7976 to **0.8476** so far, measured on a full-suite grade of main. Two fixes made the gain:

| Change | Overall | Per-test effect |
|---|---|---|
| Phase 4 milestone | 0.7976 | |
| Display starts blank (white), like the reference | 0.7980 | every replay up slightly, none down |
| DMA copy no longer cancelled by the next instruction | **0.8476** | goodboy video 0.081 → **1.0** |

The DMA fix is the big one. goodboy's level loader starts a DMA copy and cancels it in the next instruction. Our one-instruction start delay let the cancel win, so its level tiles never loaded. The reference completes the copy. goodboy's audio slipped from 0.951 to 0.916, probably because the level now plays its real music, which our mixer matches less closely.

Still running:
- **spout** (video 0.286): CPU instruction cycle timing, because its gameplay drifts out of sync early.
- **heartwrench** (video 0.577): the cartridge prefetch buffer, because it drifts out of sync from about frame 2900.

The Phase 4 milestone was 0.7976, so the gate's "overall above the latest milestone" part is already met. The other part, no replay more than 0.02 below its previous score, also holds so far. I'll check both again when the two workers report.

The goodboy problem was one clear bug. These two games drift because of accumulated cycle timing. Each timing change moves several things at once, so the workers are trading one error for another. That's slow, iterative work with diminishing returns. A wrong timing model can also hurt replays that score 0.99 today.

My recommendation is to let both finish their current runs, then merge only what is a net win on the full suite, under the gate rule that no replay drops by more than 0.02. - `c413183 feat(cpu): charge pipeline refill fetches on R15 writes and exceptions`: in `step()` (`/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/.claude/worktrees/agent-a874da11c32c210d1/src/cpu/mod.rs`), any instruction that writes R15 (branch, BX, ALU or LDR/LDM to PC, SWI, undefined), and IRQ entry, now cost one extra fetch of the target, which is always charged as non-sequential. content.text:
Phase 5 is closed and tagged `phase-5` after one round, as you chose. Nothing has been pushed.

**Score row** (commit `a31eece`):

| | Overall | Replay | Procedural | Audio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Phase 5 | **0.8476** | **0.8648** | 0.7611 | 0.8827 |
| Phase 4 | 0.7976 | 0.7806 | 0.7611 | 0.8852 |
| Baseline | 0.5345 | 0.596 | 0.486 | 0.399 |

The gate passes: overall is above Phase 4, no replay's video score dropped, and no procedural test changed. The top possible score is 0.96.

One audio score fell by more than 0.02: goodboy, from 0.951 to 0.916. Its level now actually loads and plays its real music. The gate counts video scores for replays, so I accepted it and logged it.

**What this phase changed:**
- **DMA start (biggest gain):** an immediate DMA now runs before the next instruction can cancel it. The goodboy worker traced the bug to the DMA code, which was outside its assigned files, so I applied the fix. goodboy video went from 0.081 to 1.0.
- **Display at power-on:** the display now starts blank (white), like the reference. Every replay rose slightly.
- **SRAM size:** cartridges that declare SRAM now get 32 KiB of save memory, mirrored. The score didn't change, but it matches gbatek.

**Agents** (all claude-opus-5-5):
- **goodboy worker:** found the DMA bug but made no commits, since the cause was outside its files.
- **spout worker:** its branch-timing change was not merged, because spout improved but heartwrench dropped by 0.12. I hard-stopped it after it kept trying variants.
- **heartwrench worker:** only the SRAM change was merged. Its cartridge prefetch buffer raised heartwrench audio from 0.55 to 0.93 but lowered video by 0.022, so it is kept on a separate branch.
- **Reviewers:** three fresh reviews in total.

**Process change, at your request:** `CLAUDE.md` now has a grading budget. Each worker gets at most 5 grader runs per task, graders run one at a time behind a shared lock, and then the worker commits its best version and reports. Procedure A requires stating this budget in every worker's task.

**Still open:**
- **Weakest replays:** spout 0.29, heartwrench 0.58 and celeste 0.73. All three drift out of sync over time because of cycle timing.
- **Best next step:** combine the CPU's branch-timing change with the prefetch buffer. Each makes things worse alone, but together they matched heartwrench's first 900 frames exactly. Both are kept on unmerged branches: `phase5/spout-gameplay` and `phase5/heartwrench-prefetch`.
- **A lead:** the reference may read the keys at the start of VBlank. Doing that made spout's intro match exactly.

Ready for Prompt 6.

content.text:
I've measured the fuel baseline, and it shows the Phase 6 gate fails today. With the fuel limit halved to 250M instructions per frame (the 2x-headroom check), varooom-3d hits the limit and its video score falls from 0.989 to 0.046. That means it has less than 2x headroom.

Native timing alone pointed the wrong way: spout is slowest natively at 16.2 ms per frame, but varooom is the one that runs out of fuel.

One `perf-hardening` worker is now running on `phase6/perf-hardening`:
- **Hot paths it may change:** CPU, bus, IO, PPU, APU, timers, DMA and the frame loop. Behaviour must not change: every score must stay within 0.005 of Phase 5.
- **Determinism test:** it also adds the test that runs 100 frames, resets, runs 100 more and compares the frames.
- **Budget:** 5 grader runs, serialised with the lock.

The baseline is logged in `NOTES.md`.

## 1. What I built and the commits
Branch `phase6/perf-hardening`, starting from 78c6836:
- `e21d97e perf(cpu): defer component stepping until the next event`
- `c3545bf test(abi): emu_reset reproduces emu_load_rom frames and audio`
- `052fa9c perf(bus): one bounds check per little-endian memory access`

**Measuring first:** `perf` is blocked on this machine (`perf_event_paranoid=4`) and there's no valgrind. So I wrote a fuel meter: a node script that rewrites the wasm so a counter adds one per executed instruction, then plays a replay and reports per-frame fuel and a per-function breakdown. It reads about 17–29% lower than the grader: varooom's frame 4 reads 213M on it and traps at 250M in the grader, while spout reads 194M and does not trap. It showed that about 75% of the fuel went into stepping the PPU, timers and APU after every single instruction.

**Main change (`e21d97e`):**
- **Deferred stepping:** `run_frame` now saves up each step's cycles in `bus.deferred_component_cycles` instead of stepping the PPU, timers and APU after every instruction. It catches them all up once the total reaches the next point where one of them can do something visible: HBlank or line start, a timer overflow, or an APU output sample.
- **IO accesses:** every IO read or write calls `Bus::catch_up_components()` first, so the CPU always sees current state. It also forces a fresh check at the end of that step, since the write may change when the next event happens.
- **Why output can't change:** no event can fall inside the saved-up cycles, and stepping a component once by a sum gives the same state as stepping it by each part. IRQs, DMA triggers, FIFO pops and samples therefore happen at the same step boundaries as before.
- **Halt:** a halted CPU still idles in chunks of at most 16 cycles, as before. `halted_cycles` now adds the saved-up cycles to the PPU's line position.
- **PSG:** the sound channels are stepped only when a sample is mixed or a sound register is accessed.
- **Event lookups:** `advance_components` is now a free function in `gba.rs`. Each component got a small helper that says how many cycles remain until its next event: `Ppu::cycles_until_line_event`, `Timers::cycles_until_overflow`, `Apu::cycles_until_sample`.

**Proof of no behaviour change:** a native runner hashed every frame's framebuffer and every audio sample across all 21 replays, before and after. The hashes are identical.

Phase 6 is closed and tagged `phase-6`, which completes the plan. All seven phases (0-6) are tagged, and nothing has been pushed.

**Phase 6 gate passed:**
- **Scores:** unchanged from Phase 5. The largest difference on any test is 0.0.
- **Determinism:** the new reset test passes. It runs 100 frames after load, resets, runs 100 frames again, and checks every frame and audio sample matches.
- **Fuel headroom:** the full suite runs at half the fuel limit (250M instead of 500M per frame) with no traps and the same overall score. Before this phase, varooom trapped at that level and its video score fell to 0.046.

**What changed:** the `perf-hardening` worker found that about 75% of the work went into stepping the PPU, timers and APU after every single instruction. Now they catch up only when one of them can actually do something: start a new line, overflow a timer or produce a sample. They also catch up whenever the game touches an IO register.
- The output is identical by construction. The worker checked it by hashing every frame and sample on all replays. The reviewer separately compared the output of 76 ROMs byte for byte.
- The heaviest frame dropped from about 342M to about 108M instructions on the worker's own fuel meter. That meter reads 17-29% low, so about 140M in the grader's terms.
- Native time per frame roughly halved.

The worker used one of its five grader runs.

**All milestone rows (`scores.tsv`):**

| Phase | Commit | Overall | Replay | Procedural | Audio | Main change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | db2cba4 | 0.1303 | 0.1143 | 0.3083 | 0.0000 | CPU |
| 2 | 8d55cb9 | 0.4326 | 0.4673 | 0.7611 | 0.0000 | Interrupts/halt, timers, DMA, bus |
| 3 | 9f4a767 | 0.6213 | 0.7818 | 0.7611 | 0.0000 | Sprites, rotated/scaled backgrounds, effects |
| 4 | e551e06 | 0.7976 | 0.7806 | 0.7611 | 0.8852 | Sound |
| 5 | a31eece | 0.8476 | 0.8648 | 0.7611 | 0.8827 | DMA start fix (goodboy), display start state, SRAM size |
| 6 | b556f0e | **0.8476** | **0.8648** | **0.7611** | **0.8827** | Performance, determinism test |

Phase 0 had no full grade. The final score of 0.8476 is against a baseline of 0.5345 and a reachable maximum of 0.96. All three sections beat the baseline (replay 0.596, procedural 0.486, audio 0.399).

**What remains:**
- **Weakest replays:** spout (video 0.29, audio 0.20), heartwrench (video 0.58, audio 0.55) and celeste (video 0.73). All three drift out of sync with the reference over time because of cycle timing.
- **Best lead for them:** combine the CPU's branch-refill cycles with the cartridge prefetch buffer. Each makes things worse alone, but together they matched heartwrench's first 900 frames exactly. Both are kept on unmerged branches: `phase5/spout-gameplay` and `phase5/heartwrench-prefetch`.
- **Second lead:** read keys at the start of VBlank. Doing that made spout's whole intro match.
- **Audio:** piugba is at 0.68, and our output runs about 957 samples longer than the reference for unknown reasons. goodboy audio fell from 0.951 to 0.916 now that its level really plays.
- **Procedural ceiling:** `mgba-multiply-long` is a loss you accepted, because gbatek gives no rule for the carry flag after a multiply. Procedural is 0.7611 out of a possible 0.8.
- **Deferred minor review items, all in `NOTES.md`:**
  - No FLASH or EEPROM save chips yet, only SRAM.
  - The ROM-detection test silently passes when its test ROM is missing.
  - A few readability and test-coverage items.
- **Worth adding to `scripts/`:** the worker's local fuel meter. It currently lives in my session scratchpad.

# GBA Eval Quickstart

This directory contains scripts and files allowing you to either:

1. **Run your own agent in the same container** the benchmark's agents
   saw — `docker compose up -d && ./shell.sh`
2. **Grade a wasm you or an agent produce** — `./grade.sh path/to/my.wasm`

## Zero-to-score (most users start here)

```bash
# from repo root, after cloning
git submodule update --init --recursive
git lfs install && git lfs pull          # pulls corpus/reference-cache/

./quickstart/smoke-test.sh                # 30s preflight — should print all ✓
./quickstart/grade.sh candidates/gba-core/gba_core_shim.wasm baseline
```

First grade: 5-10 min cold (docker builds `gba-eval-grader` the first
time it runs). Subsequent grades: seconds to a minute, depending on
whether the reference cache is warm.

Output lands in `./results/baseline/` — per-testcase JSON, PNG
screenshots, and `summary.json` with the overall score.

## Requirements

Pick one path:

- **Docker (default)** — docker and docker compose.
- **Native (`--native`)** — Rust 1.87, clang, cmake, and a one-time
  `reference/build-mesen.sh native`. Use this if you're hacking on the
  grader.

Either way you also need `git-lfs` for `corpus/reference-cache/`
(~230 MB pull, 51 precomputed reference frames). `smoke-test.sh` will
tell you if LFS didn't fire.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copy this project's Claude Code session transcripts into logs/, redacting
# credentials, API keys, tokens and email addresses, and write logs/README.md.
#
#   scripts/export-logs.sh            # reads ${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-~/.claude}/projects
#
# Sessions exported (found by ID in any project folder):
#   architect  005f9e94-f8e5-4ebe-a362-77fc748b7f0d  wrote PLAN.md, CLAUDE.md, agents, EXECUTOR_PROMPTS.md
#   executor   ec739230-fb4b-467b-9709-e53c38e370f4  ran phases 0-6, plus its subagents/ folder
#   abandoned  56c254ce-954b-416f-9898-b892d2cdf4b7  first attempt, abandoned
# Run it last: the executor transcript keeps growing while that session is open.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
PROJECTS="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/projects"
OUT="$ROOT/logs"
[ -d "$PROJECTS" ] || { echo "error: $PROJECTS not found (set CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR)" >&2; exit 1; }
mkdir -p "$OUT"

python3 -I - "$PROJECTS" "$OUT" <<'PY'
import json, pathlib, re, sys

projects, out = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]), pathlib.Path(sys.argv[2])
SESSIONS = [
    ("architect", "005f9e94-f8e5-4ebe-a362-77fc748b7f0d",
     "Architect session (terminal 2): wrote PLAN.md, CLAUDE.md, the agent definitions and EXECUTOR_PROMPTS.md."),
    ("executor", "ec739230-fb4b-467b-9709-e53c38e370f4",
     "Executor session (terminal 3): ran phases 0-6 as integrator, launched worker and reviewer agents."),
    ("abandoned", "56c254ce-954b-416f-9898-b892d2cdf4b7",
     "First session, abandoned before the plan was finalised."),
]

# Only secrets are redacted. Each pattern has a label used in the README counts.
PATTERNS = [
    ("anthropic-api-key", re.compile(r"sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{10,}")),
    ("openai-style-key", re.compile(r"\bsk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}\b")),
    ("github-token", re.compile(r"\b(?:ghp|gho|ghu|ghs|ghr)_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}\b|\bgithub_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,}\b")),
    ("aws-access-key", re.compile(r"\bAKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}\b")),
    ("slack-token", re.compile(r"\bxox[abprs]-[A-Za-z0-9\-]{10,}\b")),
    ("bearer-token", re.compile(r"(?i)\bbearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._\-]{16,}")),
    ("jwt", re.compile(r"\beyJ[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{10,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{10,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{10,}")),
    # key=value style secrets: the value must look like a secret (16+ chars, no spaces).
    ("credential-assignment", re.compile(
        r"(?i)\b(api[_-]?key|access[_-]?token|auth[_-]?token|refresh[_-]?token|secret|password|passwd)"
        r"(\\?[\"']?\s*[:=]\s*\\?[\"']?)([A-Za-z0-9/+_.\-]{16,})")),
    ("email", re.compile(r"\b[A-Za-z0-9._%+\-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.\-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}\b")),
]

def redact(text, counts):
    for label, pattern in PATTERNS:
        def replace(match):
            counts[label] = counts.get(label, 0) + 1
            if label == "credential-assignment":
                return match.group(1) + match.group(2) + "[REDACTED:credential]"
            return f"[REDACTED:{label}]"
        text = pattern.sub(replace, text)
    return text

def find(session_id):
    hits = sorted(projects.glob(f"*/{session_id}.jsonl"))
    if not hits:
        sys.exit(f"error: transcript {session_id}.jsonl not found under {projects}")
    return hits[0]

rows = []
for role, session_id, description in SESSIONS:
    source = find(session_id)
    sources = [(source, out / f"{role}-{session_id[:8]}.jsonl", description)]
    subagents = source.parent / session_id / "subagents"
    if subagents.is_dir():
        for path in sorted(subagents.iterdir()):
            if path.is_file():
                target = out / f"{role}-{session_id[:8]}-subagents" / path.name
                sources.append((path, target, f"Subagent of the {role} session ({path.suffix[1:]})"))
    for src, dst, what in sources:
        counts = {}
        dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        dst.write_text(redact(src.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"), counts), encoding="utf-8")
        rows.append((dst.relative_to(out), what, counts))
        print(f"{dst.relative_to(out)}: " + (", ".join(f"{k} x{v}" for k, v in counts.items()) or "nothing redacted"))

lines = [
    "# Claude Code session logs",
    "",
    "Exported by `scripts/export-logs.sh` from the local Claude Code transcripts (JSONL, one event per line).",
    "Only secrets were redacted: credentials, API keys, tokens and email addresses, replaced by",
    "`[REDACTED:<kind>]`. Nothing else was changed or removed. Token usage per session is in `usage.md`",
    "(`scripts/token-usage.sh`).",
    "",
    "| File | What it is | Redacted |",

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Sum token usage per session from exported transcripts into logs/usage.md.
#
#   scripts/token-usage.sh [logs-dir]      # default: logs/ (run scripts/export-logs.sh first)
#
# Each API response is counted once (deduplicated by message id; a response that is
# split over several transcript lines repeats the same usage). Subagent transcripts
# are summed into their parent session and also listed on their own.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
LOGS="${1:-$ROOT/logs}"
[ -d "$LOGS" ] || { echo "error: $LOGS not found; run scripts/export-logs.sh first" >&2; exit 1; }

python3 -I - "$LOGS" <<'PY'
import collections, json, pathlib, sys

logs = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
FIELDS = ["input_tokens", "cache_creation_input_tokens", "cache_read_input_tokens", "output_tokens"]

def usage_of(path):
    """Token totals and model counts for one transcript, one entry per message id."""
    totals, models, seen = collections.Counter(), collections.Counter(), set()
    for line in path.open(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"):
        try:
            event = json.loads(line)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        message = event.get("message") if isinstance(event, dict) else None
        if event.get("type") != "assistant" or not isinstance(message, dict) or "usage" not in message:
            continue
        key = message.get("id") or event.get("requestId") or event.get("uuid")
        if key in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(key)
        for field in FIELDS:
            totals[field] += message["usage"].get(field) or 0
        models[message.get("model", "unknown")] += 1
    totals["responses"] = len(seen)
    return totals, models

def row(name, totals):
    cells = [f"{totals[f]:,}" for f in FIELDS + ["responses"]]
    total = sum(totals[f] for f in FIELDS)
    return f"| {name} | " + " | ".join(cells) + f" | {total:,} |"

header = ["| Transcript | Input | Cache write | Cache read | Output | Responses | All tokens |",
          "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
sessions, details = [], []
for main in sorted(logs.glob("*.jsonl")):
    totals, models = usage_of(main)
    sub_dir = logs / (main.stem + "-subagents")
    sub_rows = []
    if sub_dir.is_dir():
        for sub in sorted(sub_dir.glob("*.jsonl")):
            sub_totals, sub_models = usage_of(sub)
            totals.update(sub_totals)
            models.update(sub_models)
            sub_rows.append(row(f"{sub_dir.name}/{sub.name}", sub_totals))
    sessions.append(row(main.stem + (" (incl. subagents)" if sub_rows else ""), totals))
    sessions[-1] += "  " + ", ".join(f"{m}: {n}" for m, n in models.most_common())
    if sub_rows:
        details += [f"### {main.stem} subagents", ""] + header + sub_rows + [""]

text = ["# Token usage per session", "",
        "Summed from the exported transcripts by `scripts/token-usage.sh`. Each API response counted once.",
        "\"All tokens\" = input + cache write + cache read + output; models and response counts follow each row.", ""]
text += header + sessions + [""] + details
(logs / "usage.md").write_text("\n".join(text) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
print("\n".join(text))
PY

    ("aws-access-key", re.compile(r"\bAKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}\b")),
    ("slack-token", re.compile(r"\bxox[abprs]-[A-Za-z0-9\-]{10,}\b")),
    ("bearer-token", re.compile(r"(?i)\bbearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._\-]{16,}")),
    ("jwt", re.compile(r"\beyJ[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{10,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{10,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{10,}")),
    # key=value style secrets: the value must look like a secret (16+ chars, no spaces).
    ("credential-assignment", re.compile(
        r"(?i)\b(api[_-]?key|access[_-]?token|auth[_-]?token|refresh[_-]?token|secret|password|passwd)"
        r"(\\?[\"']?\s*[:=]\s*\\?[\"']?)([A-Za-z0-9/+_.\-]{16,})")),
    ("email", re.compile(r"\b[A-Za-z0-9._%+\-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.\-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}\b")),
]

def redact(text, counts):
    for label, pattern in PATTERNS:
        def replace(match):
            counts[label] = counts.get(label, 0) + 1
            if label == "credential-assignment":
                return match.group(1) + match.group(2) + "[REDACTED:credential]"
            return f"[REDACTED:{label}]"
        text = pattern.sub(replace, text)
    return text

def find(session_id):
    hits = sorted(projects.glob(f"*/{session_id}.jsonl"))
    if not hits:
        sys.exit(f"error: transcript {session_id}.jsonl not found under {projects}")
    return hits[0]

rows = []
for role, session_id, description in SESSIONS:
    source = find(session_id)
    sources = [(source, out / f"{role}-{session_id[:8]}.jsonl", description)]
    subagents = source.parent / session_id / "subagents"
    if subagents.is_dir():
        for path in sorted(subagents.iterdir()):
            if path.is_file():
                target = out / f"{role}-{session_id[:8]}-subagents" / path.name
                sources.append((path, target, f"Subagent of the {role} session ({path.suffix[1:]})"))
    for src, dst, what in sources:
        counts = {}
        dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        dst.write_text(redact(src.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"), counts), encoding="utf-8")
        rows.append((dst.relative_to(out), what, counts))
        print(f"{dst.relative_to(out)}: " + (", ".join(f"{k} x{v}" for k, v in counts.items()) or "nothing redacted"))

lines = [
    "# Claude Code session logs",
    "",
    "Exported by `scripts/export-logs.sh` from the local Claude Code transcripts (JSONL, one event per line).",
    "Only secrets were redacted: credentials, API keys, tokens and email addresses, replaced by",
    "`[REDACTED:<kind>]`. Nothing else was changed or removed. Token usage per session is in `usage.md`",
    "(`scripts/token-usage.sh`).",
    "",
    "| File | What it is | Redacted |",
    "|---|---|---|",
]
for path, what, counts in rows:
    redacted = ", ".join(f"{k} x{v}" for k, v in sorted(counts.items())) or "nothing"
    lines.append(f"| `{path}` | {what} | {redacted} |")
(out / "README.md").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
print(f"wrote {out / 'README.md'}")
PY

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Sum token usage per session from exported transcripts into logs/usage.md.
#
#   scripts/token-usage.sh [logs-dir]      # default: logs/ (run scripts/export-logs.sh first)
#
# Each API response is counted once (deduplicated by message id; a response that is
# split over several transcript lines repeats the same usage). Subagent transcripts
# are summed into their parent session and also listed on their own.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
LOGS="${1:-$ROOT/logs}"
[ -d "$LOGS" ] || { echo "error: $LOGS not found; run scripts/export-logs.sh first" >&2; exit 1; }

python3 -I - "$LOGS" <<'PY'
import collections, json, pathlib, sys

logs = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
FIELDS = ["input_tokens", "cache_creation_input_tokens", "cache_read_input_tokens", "output_tokens"]

def usage_of(path):
    """Token totals and model counts for one transcript, one entry per message id."""
    totals, models, seen = collections.Counter(), collections.Counter(), set()
    for line in path.open(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"):
        try:
            event = json.loads(line)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        message = event.get("message") if isinstance(event, dict) else None
        if event.get("type") != "assistant" or not isinstance(message, dict) or "usage" not in message:
            continue
        key = message.get("id") or event.get("requestId") or event.get("uuid")
        if key in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(key)
        for field in FIELDS:
            totals[field] += message["usage"].get(field) or 0
        models[message.get("model", "unknown")] += 1
    totals["responses"] = len(seen)
    return totals, models

def row(name, totals):
    cells = [f"{totals[f]:,}" for f in FIELDS + ["responses"]]
    total = sum(totals[f] for f in FIELDS)
    return f"| {name} | " + " | ".join(cells) + f" | {total:,} |"

header = ["| Transcript | Input | Cache write | Cache read | Output | Responses | All tokens |",
          "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
sessions, details = [], []
for main in sorted(logs.glob("*.jsonl")):
    totals, models = usage_of(main)
    sub_dir = logs / (main.stem + "-subagents")
    sub_rows = []
    if sub_dir.is_dir():
        for sub in sorted(sub_dir.glob("*.jsonl")):
            sub_totals, sub_models = usage_of(sub)
            totals.update(sub_totals)
            models.update(sub_models)
            sub_rows.append(row(f"{sub_dir.name}/{sub.name}", sub_totals))
    sessions.append(row(main.stem + (" (incl. subagents)" if sub_rows else ""), totals))
    sessions[-1] += "  " + ", ".join(f"{m}: {n}" for m, n in models.most_common())
    if sub_rows:
        details += [f"### {main.stem} subagents", ""] + header + sub_rows + [""]

text = ["# Token usage per session", "",
        "Summed from the exported transcripts by `scripts/token-usage.sh`. Each API response counted once.",
        "\"All tokens\" = input + cache write + cache read + output; models and response counts follow each row.", ""]
text += header + sessions + [""] + details
(logs / "usage.md").write_text("\n".join(text) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
print("\n".join(text))
PY

input.content:
# gba-emu

An original Game Boy Advance emulator in Rust, compiled to `wasm32-unknown-unknown` and graded by the
[gba-eval](https://github.com/mechanize-work/gba-eval) benchmark against the Mesen2 reference. It was built
by Claude Code agents (model `claude-opus-5-5`) working from a written plan, with every change reviewed by a
separate agent before it was merged.

**Submission version: tag `phase-6`** (code at commit `b556f0e`). The prebuilt wasm is in
[`dist/gba_emu.wasm`](dist/gba_emu.wasm), with its checksum in [`dist/SHA256SUMS`](dist/SHA256SUMS). It is
byte-identical to a fresh build of the tag.

## Score

Full grader runs, one per milestone (`scores.tsv`, details in `results/milestones/phase-N/summary.json`):

| Milestone | Commit | Overall | Replay | Procedural | Audio | Main change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline (gba-core) | — | 0.5345 | 0.596 | 0.486 | 0.399 | reference point given by the benchmark |
| phase-1 | db2cba4 | 0.1303 | 0.1143 | 0.3083 | 0.0000 | CPU (ARM + THUMB) and basic display |
| phase-2 | 8d55cb9 | 0.4326 | 0.4673 | 0.7611 | 0.0000 | Interrupts/halt, timers, DMA, bus wait states, open bus |
| phase-3 | 9f4a767 | 0.6213 | 0.7818 | 0.7611 | 0.0000 | Sprites, affine/bitmap BGs, windows, blending, mosaic |
| phase-4 | e551e06 | 0.7976 | 0.7806 | 0.7611 | 0.8852 | Sound: PSG channels, FIFO A/B, mixer |
| phase-5 | a31eece | 0.8476 | 0.8648 | 0.7611 | 0.8827 | Compatibility: DMA start timing, display power-on, SRAM |
| **phase-6** | **b556f0e** | **0.8476** | **0.8648** | **0.7611** | **0.8827** | Performance (2x fuel headroom), reset determinism |
| Ceiling | — | 0.96 | 1.0 | 0.8 | 1.0 | the `comprehensive` subsystem has weight but no tests |

Phase 0 (skeleton) has no full grade. Every section of the final version beats the baseline. 15 of the 16
procedural tests score 1.0; the exception is `mgba-multiply-long` (see "Changes of approach").

## Setup

Tools used (versions on the build machine):

| Tool | Version |
|---|---|
| rustc / cargo | 1.99.1, with target `wasm32-unknown-unknown` |
| Docker | 29.7.2 (runs the `gba-eval-grader` image) |
| git / git-lfs | 2.43.0 / 3.4.1 (gba-eval keeps its reference cache in LFS) |
| Python 3 | used by the scripts (standard library only) |
| Claude Code | 2.1.318, model `claude-opus-5-5`; only needed to rerun the agent workflow |

Lay the two repos out so gba-eval is at `../../gba-eval` relative to this repo, or set `GBA_EVAL`:

```bash
mkdir work && cd work
git clone https://github.com/mechanize-work/gba-eval
(cd gba-eval && git submodule update --init --recursive && git lfs install && git lfs pull)
mkdir trial && git clone https://github.com/Rohan-Jalil/gba-eval-trial-rohan trial/gba-emu
cd trial/gba-emu
rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown
# or, for any other layout: export GBA_EVAL=/absolute/path/to/gba-eval
```

Build and test:

```bash
cargo test                                                    # 129 unit tests, incl. reset determinism
cargo build --release --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown   # -> target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/gba_emu.wasm
cargo run --release --bin run_rom -- <rom.gba> <frames> out.ppm [out.wav]   # native debug runner
```

The first grade builds the `gba-eval-grader` docker image (see gba-eval's `quickstart/README.md`).

## Grading

```bash
# Full grade (~10 min): builds, grades, appends to scores.tsv, saves results/milestones/<name>/
scripts/grade-full.sh phase-x "note"

# Subset: only the named testcases, results in results/<run-name>/ (read the per-testcase lines)
scripts/grade-subset.sh target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/gba_emu.wasm my-run memory aw-arm-alu tonc-snd1
```

Run graders one at a time; parallel graders can run the machine out of memory (wrap them in
`flock /tmp/gba-emu-grader.lock ...`).

**Verify independently.** Build any milestone tag and grade it with gba-eval's own script, without this repo's
scripts:

```bash
git checkout phase-6        # or phase-1 ... phase-5
cargo build --release --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown
"$GBA_EVAL/quickstart/grade.sh" "$PWD/target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/gba_emu.wasm" gba-emu-phase-6
# or grade the committed artifact: "$GBA_EVAL/quickstart/grade.sh" "$PWD/dist/gba_emu.wasm" gba-emu-dist
sha256sum -c dist/SHA256SUMS   # from dist/
```

## Repository layout

```
src/                 the emulator (see Architecture)
src/bin/run_rom.rs   native runner: N frames of a ROM to .ppm (+ .wav)
assets/              gba_bios_stub.bin, copied from gba-eval/spec (embedded with include_bytes!)
dist/                release wasm of tag phase-6 + SHA256SUMS
scripts/             grade-full.sh, grade-subset.sh, gba-eval-path.sh (default GBA_EVAL),
                     export-logs.sh, token-usage.sh
results/milestones/  summary.json and score row of each full grade (other results/ output is ignored)
scores.tsv           one row per milestone
PLAN.md              the build plan: scoring analysis, architecture and contracts, phases, workflow, risks
CLAUDE.md            binding rules for every agent: originality, readability, ownership, git, grading budget
EXECUTOR_PROMPTS.md  the prompt for each phase and Procedures A (worker) and B (milestone)
NOTES.md             decision log (date, what, why) and the agent/model used per phase
TIMELOG.md           my own hours
.claude/agents/      one definition per worker role, plus `reviewer`
.claude/settings.json  deny rules (other emulators' source, web access, git push)
logs/                exported Claude Code transcripts and token usage (after scripts/export-logs.sh)
```

## Architecture

One crate, `gba_emu`, built as `cdylib` (the wasm) and `rlib` (native tests and `run_rom`). Each subsystem
lives in its own file, so parallel agents never edited the same file:

| File | Component |
|---|---|
| `lib.rs` | the 10 ABI exports (`spec/ABI.md`), thin wrappers over one global `Gba`; ROM, framebuffer and audio buffers live outside `Gba` so their pointers stay valid |
| `gba.rs` | `Gba`: CPU + bus, `run_frame` main loop, event routing between components |
| `bus.rs` | memory map, 8/16/32-bit access, wait states (WAITCNT, sequential/non-sequential), open bus, BIOS protection |
| `io.rs` | IO register dispatch by address range, readable-bit masks, 8/32-bit split and merge |
| `irq.rs` | IE/IF/IME, `request(IrqSource)`, HALTCNT |
| `cpu/` | `mod.rs` registers, modes, banking, exceptions, `step`; `alu.rs` shifter and flags; `arm.rs`, `thumb.rs` decoders |
| `ppu/` | `mod.rs` line timing, DISPCNT/DISPSTAT, affine reference points; `bg_text.rs`, `bg_affine.rs`, `bitmap.rs`, `obj.rs` layer renderers; `effects.rs` the compositor (windows, blending, mosaic) |
| `apu/` | `mod.rs` mixer, SOUNDBIAS, sample rate; `psg.rs` channels 1-4; `fifo.rs` direct sound A/B |
| `timer.rs`, `dma.rs`, `keypad.rs`, `cart.rs` | timers, 4 DMA channels, KEYINPUT/KEYCNT, ROM and SRAM |

Shared contracts, fixed in Phase 0 and changed only by the integrator:

- **Bus:** the CPU only talks to the bus (`read8/16/32`, `write8/16/32`); each access adds its cycle cost,
  drained by the CPU per instruction. The bus owns every component except the CPU.
- **IO:** owners expose `io_read16(offset)` and `io_write16(offset, value, mask)`, where the mask marks
  the bytes really written (a read-modify-write would break IF acknowledge, HALTCNT and the FIFOs).
- **Interrupts:** any component calls `irq.request(source)`; only the CPU consumes them.
- **Timing:** `run_frame` runs 280,896 cycles (228 lines x 1232) from line 0 through VBlank, measured to
  match Mesen2's frame boundary; `emu_load_rom`/`emu_reset` run 5 hidden frames so frame 0 lines up with the
  reference (the grader burns 6 warm-up frames on Mesen2 and none on us). Since Phase 6, PPU, timers and APU
  are caught up only at their next event or on an IO access, with identical results.
- **Events:** PPU HBlank/VBlank to DMA, timer overflow to the FIFOs, FIFO refill to DMA, all as plain
  method calls in `gba.rs`.
- **Graphics:** every layer renders one scanline into `[LayerPixel; 240]` (`LineLayers`); only the
  compositor merges them.
- **Audio:** output at Mesen2's rate, `32768 << SOUNDBIAS bits 14-15`, with an exact sample count per frame.

## Workflow

Three Claude Code sessions, all on `claude-opus-5-5`:

1. **Supervisor (private).** It taught me the domain, drafted the prompts for the other two sessions,
   reviewed their transcripts and recommended decisions. Prompts that appear as pasted text in the other
   sessions' logs came from this session.
2. **Architect (terminal 2).** It studied gba-eval and wrote `PLAN.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, the agent definitions in
   `.claude/agents/`, `EXECUTOR_PROMPTS.md` and the grading scripts.
3. **Executor (terminal 3).** It acted as the integrator and ran Phases 0-6 from `EXECUTOR_PROMPTS.md`:
   - it launched parallel worker agents, each in its own git worktree and branch (`phaseN/<role>`), owning only its files;
   - it merged a branch only after a fresh `reviewer` agent with no author context had checked it against gbatek, the ownership rules and for signs of copied code;
   - each merge passed `cargo test`, the wasm build and the smoke set, and each phase ended with a full grade and a tag.

[PLACEHOLDER: say here whether the supervisor session log is included.]

Every branch, including failed and unmerged attempts, is kept in the history: for example
`phase5/spout-gameplay` and `phase5/heartwrench-prefetch`. The worktrees have been removed.

### Agents, skills and prompts

- **Agent definitions:** `.claude/agents/*.md`, one per worker role (skeleton-builder, cpu-core, cpu-arm, cpu-thumb,
  ppu-basic, irq-halt, timers, dma, ppu-sprites, ppu-affine-bitmap, ppu-effects, apu-psg, apu-fifo-mixer,
  compat-timing, perf-hardening) plus `reviewer`.

One crate, `gba_emu`, built as `cdylib` (the wasm) and `rlib` (native tests and `run_rom`). Each subsystem
lives in its own file, so parallel agents never edited the same file:

| File | Component |
|---|---|
| `lib.rs` | the 10 ABI exports (`spec/ABI.md`), thin wrappers over one global `Gba`; ROM, framebuffer and audio buffers live outside `Gba` so their pointers stay valid |

| `ppu/` | `mod.rs` line timing, DISPCNT/DISPSTAT, affine reference points; `bg_text.rs`, `bg_affine.rs`, `bitmap.rs`, `obj.rs` layer renderers; `effects.rs` the compositor (windows, blending, mosaic) |
| `apu/` | `mod.rs` mixer, SOUNDBIAS, sample rate; `psg.rs` channels 1-4; `fifo.rs` direct sound A/B |
| `timer.rs`, `dma.rs`, `keypad.rs`, `cart.rs` | timers, 4 DMA channels, KEYINPUT/KEYCNT, ROM and SRAM |

Shared contracts, fixed in Phase 0 and changed only by the integrator:

  method calls in `gba.rs`.
- **Graphics:** every layer renders one scanline into `[LayerPixel; 240]` (`LineLayers`); only the

| `ppu/` | `mod.rs` line timing, DISPCNT/DISPSTAT, affine reference points; `bg_text.rs`, `bg_affine.rs`, `bitmap.rs`, `obj.rs` layer renderers; `effects.rs` the compositor (windows, blending, mosaic) |
| `apu/` | `mod.rs` mixer, SOUNDBIAS, sample rate; `psg.rs` channels 1-4; `fifo.rs` direct sound A/B |
| `timer.rs`, `dma.rs`, `keypad.rs`, `cart.rs` | timers, 4 DMA channels, KEYINPUT/KEYCNT, ROM and SRAM |

Shared contracts, fixed in Phase 0 and changed only by the integrator:

- **Bus:** the CPU only talks to the bus (`read8/16/32`, `write8/16/32`); each access adds its cycle cost,
  drained by the CPU per instruction. The bus owns every component except the CPU.
- **IO:** owners expose `io_read16(offset)` and `io_write16(offset, value, mask)`, where the mask marks
  the bytes really written (a read-modify-write would break IF acknowledge, HALTCNT and the FIFOs).
- **Interrupts:** any component calls `irq.request(source)`; only the CPU consumes them.
- **Timing:** `run_frame` runs 280,896 cycles (228 lines x 1232) from line 0 through VBlank, measured to
  match Mesen2's frame boundary; `emu_load_rom`/`emu_reset` run 5 hidden frames so frame 0 lines up with the
  reference (the grader burns 6 warm-up frames on Mesen2 and none on us). Since Phase 6, PPU, timers and APU
  are caught up only at their next event or on an IO access, with identical results.
- **Events:** PPU HBlank/VBlank to DMA, timer overflow to the FIFOs, FIFO refill to DMA, all as plain
  method calls in `gba.rs`.
- **Graphics:** every layer renders one scanline into `[LayerPixel; 240]` (`LineLayers`); only the
  compositor merges them.
- **Audio:** output at Mesen2's rate, `32768 << SOUNDBIAS bits 14-15`, with an exact sample count per frame.

## Workflow

Three Claude Code sessions, all on `claude-opus-5-5`:

1. **Supervisor (private).** It taught me the domain, drafted the prompts for the other two sessions,
   reviewed their transcripts and recommended decisions. Prompts that appear as pasted text in the other
   sessions' logs came from this session.
2. **Architect (terminal 2).** It studied gba-eval and wrote `PLAN.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, the agent definitions in
   `.claude/agents/`, `EXECUTOR_PROMPTS.md` and the grading scripts.
3. **Executor (terminal 3).** It acted as the integrator and ran Phases 0-6 from `EXECUTOR_PROMPTS.md`:
   - it launched parallel worker agents, each in its own git worktree and branch (`phaseN/<role>`), owning only its files;
   - it merged a branch only after a fresh `reviewer` agent with no author context had checked it against gbatek, the ownership rules and for signs of copied code;
   - each merge passed `cargo test`, the wasm build and the smoke set, and each phase ended with a full grade and a tag.

[PLACEHOLDER: say here whether the supervisor session log is included.]

Every branch, including failed and unmerged attempts, is kept in the history: for example
`phase5/spout-gameplay` and `phase5/heartwrench-prefetch`. The worktrees have been removed.

### Agents, skills and prompts

- **Agent definitions:** `.claude/agents/*.md`, one per worker role (skeleton-builder, cpu-core, cpu-arm, cpu-thumb,
  ppu-basic, irq-halt, timers, dma, ppu-sprites, ppu-affine-bitmap, ppu-effects, apu-psg, apu-fifo-mixer,
  compat-timing, perf-hardening) plus `reviewer`.
- **Phase prompts and procedures:** `EXECUTOR_PROMPTS.md`, Prompts 0-6 and Procedures A and B.
- **Rules every agent follows:** `CLAUDE.md`.
- **Guard rails:** `.claude/settings.json` deny rules.
- **Skills:** no custom skills were written for this project.
- **Per-phase record:** `NOTES.md` lists which agents ran on which model, with review rounds and outcomes.

## Significant changes of approach

All of these are logged in `NOTES.md` with date and reason.

- **mgba gate moved (Phase 1 to 2).** The three mgba-suite CPU tests need interrupts and DMA before they can
  show anything, so they moved to the Phase 2 gate. There they pass, except multiply-long.
- **Multiply-long carry accepted as a loss.** gbatek only says the carry flag is "destroyed". A carry rule
  fitted to the test ROM's screens was flagged by review as an originality risk and removed. Cost: about
  0.008 overall.
- **Replay gate rule amended (Phase 4).** Replay came out 0.0012 below Phase 3, all of it spout's video, while
  audio went from 0 to 0.885. I accepted the exception instead of reverting to 0.62 overall.
- **Grader serialisation and grading budget.**
  - Parallel graders ran out of memory in Phase 3, so graders now run one at a time behind `flock`, and reviewers don't grade.
  - Phase 5 timing workers kept iterating, so `CLAUDE.md` now caps each worker at 5 grader runs. After that it commits its best measured version and reports.
- **Phase 5 stopped after round 1.**
  - goodboy turned out to be a DMA start-timing bug rather than graphics: its video went from 0.08 to 1.0.
  - The two timing workers' changes (CPU branch refill, cartridge prefetch) each made another replay worse on their own. They are kept on branches rather than merged.

## Known limitations and next steps

- **Weakest replays:** spout (video 0.29), heartwrench (0.58) and celeste (0.73). They drift out of sync over
  time because of cycle timing. The most promising next step is to combine CPU pipeline-refill cycles
  (gbatek 2S+1N per branch) with the Game Pak prefetch buffer: together they matched heartwrench's first 900
  frames exactly. Both are on unmerged branches.
- **Key latching:** the reference may apply key input at VBlank start. Trying that made spout's intro match
  exactly.
- **Audio:**
  - piugba audio is 0.68: our output runs about 957 samples longer, cause unknown.
  - spout and heartwrench audio follow their video drift.
- **Save hardware:** only SRAM. FLASH, EEPROM and the GPIO/rumble port are not implemented.
- **Timing model:** there is no cycle-exact scheduler.
  - The DMA start delay and IRQ entry cycles aren't charged.
  - A halted CPU wakes up to 16 cycles late.
  - Several timer and DMA constants were measured against the grader and must be re-checked if CPU timing changes.
- **Smaller review items** are deferred and listed in `NOTES.md`:
  - vertical mosaic when it is switched on partway through a block;
  - mosaic on affine layers;
  - a few readability splits.

## Originality

- **No existing emulator code was used, read or paraphrased.** All code was written by the agents from
  gbatek (the GBA, ARM and THUMB chapters in `gba-eval/spec/`), the ABI spec, the BIOS stub and the grader's
  outputs (scores, `.ref.png` vs `.cand.png`, measured behaviour of the test ROMs).
- **Guards:**
  - `CLAUDE.md` forbids reading gba-eval's baseline candidate, Mesen2 and other emulators, and forbids per-ROM hacks.
  - `.claude/settings.json` denies reads of those folders and denies web access.
  - Every branch was reviewed by a fresh agent that looked specifically for copied structure, names or tables. Two such concerns came up (a fitted multiply carry rule, Game Boy documentation details in the PSG), and both were removed.
  - The deny rules only cover Claude Code agents started from this repo, so they are a guard rail, not proof.
- **Experience:** I had no prior experience with this evaluation or with GBA emulation before this project.

## Omitted or external

- **gba-eval is not included.** That repository (grader, test corpus, ROMs, replays, reference cache, gbatek,
  `reference/mesen.wasm`) is separate and has its own licences. Clone it as described in Setup.
- **Docker** is needed to grade (the `gba-eval-grader` image).
- **A Claude Code subscription** is needed to rerun the agent workflow. Building, testing and grading need
  only the tools in Setup.
